title: Palmetto Ballot Report
description: Every race on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot for Palmetto, FL 34221: who funds each candidate, their record, and what was found.
kicker: General election · Tuesday, November 3, 2026 · polls 7am–7pm · Palmetto, FL 34221
headline: Who is on your ballot, and who is paying for them
lede: Every race a Palmetto (34221) voter can see, in ballot order. For each candidate: the money — how much, from where, from whom, and who is spending to help or hurt them — then their public record, cases and complaints, documented foreign ties, and what the owner's chosen sources say. Party is shown because it is printed on the ballot; nothing here is sorted or scored by it.

boxes.title: First: confirm which district races are on YOUR ballot
boxes.html: 34221 is split. Everyone gets the statewide, U.S. House 16, State Senate 20, county-wide and judicial races. State House (70 or 71), County Commission district, School Board district and Palmetto city races depend on your exact address. Your personal sample ballot and polling place are at votemanatee.gov/sample-ballots (name + date of birth). On Election Day you must vote at your assigned precinct. Bring photo ID with a signature.

boxes.title: How to read this
boxes.html:
This report does not tell you who to vote for. It lays out who wrote the checks and what the public record shows, so you can judge against your own three questions: commitment to the country and to this area, foreign ties, and big money that could sway them. A donation is a fact about the donor; it is not proof of what the candidate will do. Filings also miss things — dark-money groups, family money, promises.

Every claim carries a link. Controversies are labelled allegation, established, dismissed or fact-checked. Newspaper editorials are shown separately as opinion. The amber boxes hold what the owner's chosen sources (Owen Shroyer, Alex Jones, Stew Peters) say; that content is reported as they say it and has not been checked against records here.

candidates.name: Ashley Moody
candidates.bio: Appointed to the U.S. Senate by Gov. DeSantis in January 2025 (sworn in Jan 21, 2025) to fill Marco Rubio's seat. Former Florida Attorney General (2019-2025), Hillsborough County circuit judge (2007-2017), former assistant U.S. Attorney. Born in Plant City; UF law degree. Sits on HELP, Homeland Security, Judiciary, Aging committees.
candidates.local_ties: Born in Plant City (Hillsborough County); served as a Thirteenth Judicial Circuit (Hillsborough) judge. Current residence not stated in sources read; no documented Manatee-specific ties found.

record.text: As AG, kept Florida in the lawsuit to strike down the ACA; opposed felon voting-rights restoration; joined Texas v. Pennsylvania (2020 election suit); petitioned to disqualify the 2024 abortion-rights measure.

Dec 2025: voted against extending ACA premium subsidies. March 2026: voted against an Iran war powers resolution. Dec 2025: with Sen. Rick Scott urged Trump to keep the offshore drilling moratorium off Florida's coasts.
As AG (Dec 2024) wrote FEMA urging easier National Flood Insurance Program rules for families recovering from Helene and Milton.
Praised Trump's April 2025 tariff announcement ('Liberation Day'); described a $9B Senate rescissions package as an accomplishment.
Feb 2026: praised the U.S. capture of Nicolas Maduro; voiced support for initial Trump strikes in the 2026 Iran war.

money_notes.text: Ken Griffin (Citadel founder) gave $2.5M in May 2026 to the super PAC Stronger Safer Nation, which backs Moody; the PAC had raised about $12M through June and (per Reuters via Hedgeweek) spent nearly $5M in the race, mostly attacking Nixon.
Campaign has reported roughly $11M raised vs. just under $1M for Nixon (FEC figures cited by WUSF, Sept 2026).

Outside groups reported supporting her include Senate Leadership Fund and Law Enforcement for a Safer America PAC (about $520,000 in independent expenditures as of June 30, 2026, per a search-result summary).

controversies.text: Hope Florida: in 2024 Centene paid $10M to the Hope Florida Foundation alongside a Medicaid settlement; money then moved through two nonprofits to Keep Florida Clean, a political committee later chaired by James Uthmeier. A Leon County grand jury report (leaked Aug 2026) called it misappropriated and said then-Attorney General Moody knew of the plan, but indicted no one. On Oct 7, 2026 the 1st District Court of Appeal ordered the report expunged and rejected its finding that the money was diverted; a request for full-court rehearing is pending. No one has been charged.
Sept 2022 bar complaint by The 65 Project over her support for the Texas v. Pennsylvania election suit. Outcome not found.

foreign_ties.text: None documented in the public records searched (FARA filings, foreign-government payments, state-owned business, foreign-agent donors).

Associated Industries of Florida (Feb 2026), Florida Police Chiefs Association and Florida Professional Firefighters (per Prediction Edge profile), Maggie's List, Senate Conservatives Fund.

candidates.name: Byron Donalds
candidates.bio: U.S. Rep. (FL-19, Naples) since 2021; Florida House 2016-2020; former bank credit analyst, surety portfolio manager and Wells Fargo Advisors financial advisor. Born in Brooklyn; FSU graduate. Won Aug 2026 primary with 47.8%. Trump-endorsed.

record.text: Jan 7, 2021: voted to object to certification of the Electoral College vote; Jan 13, 2021: voted against impeaching Trump.

Opposed U.S. funding for Ukraine citing the deficit; voted for the 2025 reconciliation act (OBBBA) July 3, 2025; voted for the Secure America Act June 9, 2026; voted against Haitian TPS extension April 2026.
Opposes statewide data-center moratorium but favors slowing new construction and says local governments can reject them.

Pledges to push to eliminate homestead property taxes via the Tax and Budget Reform Commission if the November amendment fails; position shifted from earlier concern it would require doubling sales tax.
Says a new Hope Florida investigation is not needed (voter-guide answer).

Running mate Bryan Avila: State senator (Hialeah/Miami, SD 39) 2022 until resigning Aug 25, 2026, after eight years in the state House (2014-2022), including Speaker pro tempore. Dean of criminal justice at Doral College; captain in the Florida Army National Guard. Named Donalds' running mate Aug 25, 2026.

money_notes.text: Main vehicle: political committee Friends of Byron Donalds; campaign claims about $81.1M raised (campaign-cited Daily Caller). Jeff Yass gave $7.5M; Ken Griffin gave $10M (largest reported); Seminole Tribe $3M; Richard Uihlein $2M; GEO Group and others (Miami New Times summary).
Speaker Daniel Perez's two political committees gave $500,000 each ($1M) to Friends of Byron Donalds.

American Mission Florida, chaired by Sarasota County Property Appraiser Bill Furst, received $3M (March 4, 2026) from the national super PAC Leading The Future (donors reported: Andreessen Horowitz, Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, Greg Brockman) and put about $2M toward pro-Donalds ads; the group says it will spend $5M for him.

Reported $1M from NextEra and Duke Energy and $275,000 from TECO Holdings to his PAC; Airbnb $1M; crypto firms (Robinhood, Ripple, Elliptic, Payward) $350,000 by end of 2025. He says donations do not influence his positions and cites 46,000 donors.

Moved $1.2M from his House campaign account to Friends of Byron Donalds within two days of announcing; FEC wrote that post-announcement House contributions 'must be refunded' except for debts; he has not returned the money.

controversies.text: 1997 marijuana possession (pretrial diversion, $150 fine); 2000 no-contest plea to felony theft (bad check), record sealed and expunged.
Campaign Legal Center ethics complaint (Sept 5, 2024) alleging he failed to timely disclose 100+ stock trades (up to $1.6M) under the STOCK Act. Outcome not found.

July 2026 civil suit by Collier school board member/charter operator Kelly Mason alleges assault over a 2022 grocery-store encounter; his campaign calls it baseless and politically motivated. Pending; no ruling found.

Primary rival James Fishback claimed Donalds was under federal sex-trafficking investigation (Aug 2026). DOJ posted 'Congressman Byron Donalds is not under investigation'; Fishback retracted on Oct 29, 2026 and apologized.
CREW ethics counsel said his financial interest in Bitcoin while pushing a pro-crypto platform is a conflict of interest; campaign says it follows all laws.

races.name: Florida Amendment 1 - Budget Stabilization Fund (rainy-day fund)
races.summary: Raises the cap on the state's reserve fund from 10% to 25% of the prior year's general revenue and requires the Legislature to deposit up to $750 million a year until the fund reaches the cap (a transfer can be suspended in limited cases, e.g. if money was drawn that year, or once every five years by two-thirds vote). Needs 60%.

who_funds_yes.text: No political committee or donors found; TaxWatch notes no formal campaign.

who_funds_no.text: No political committee or donors found.

supporters.text: Republican Party of Florida (endorsed); Senate President Ben Albritton; House Speaker Daniel Perez; Florida TaxWatch (yes, 'tough call'); Democratic gubernatorial nominee David Jolly (with guardrails).

opponents.text: Gov. Ron DeSantis ('foolish'); Byron Donalds campaign spokesperson; House Democratic Leader Fentrice Driskell; Miami-Dade and Palm Beach County Democratic parties.

fiscal.text: Required deposits of $750M a year; current maximum about $5B. Florida TaxWatch estimates the fund could reach the cap around 2049 at 2.4% revenue growth (about $16.4B tied up) and might never reach it at 3% growth. No local-government revenue loss. The Legislature passed it 100-1 (House) and 29-4 (Senate).

races.name: Florida Amendment 2 - Agricultural tangible personal property tax exemption
races.summary: Exempts machinery, equipment and tools (not land or buildings) used on agricultural land or in agritourism from property tax, beginning tax year 2027; the Legislature sets details. Businesses, including farms, already get a $25,000 tangible-property exemption. Needs 60%.

who_funds_yes.text: No political committee or donors found.

who_funds_no.text: No political committee or donors found.

supporters.text: Sen. Keith Truenow and Rep. Danny Alvarez (sponsors); Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson; Florida Farm Bureau; Florida TaxWatch (yes).

fiscal.text: Legislative estimate: about $31.0M less local property-tax revenue in FY2027-28, $32.3M the next year, $33.6M the year after (statewide; larger relative impact on small rural counties). Passed 110-1 (House) and unanimously (Senate).

races.name: Florida Amendment 3 - Homestead exemption increase and limits on local property-tax spending ('Save Our Homes From Excessive Property Taxes')
races.summary: Raises the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 (inflation-indexed after), lets local governments raise it further, cuts the yearly assessment-growth cap for non-homestead property from 10% to 5% (non-school), makes people who establish Florida residency after Dec 31, 2026 wait five years for the full exemption, and limits what local governments may spend property-tax revenue on. School taxes are excluded. Needs 60%; takes effect Jan 1, 2027.

Manatee County: REC-based estimate of nearly $68M (FY2027-28) and $127.5M (FY2028-29); City of Palmetto $1.39M and Bradenton $5.2M in FY2027-28 (as reported by Tampa Bay Beacons). A Florida Policy Institute calculator figure of about $212M for Manatee in year one was reported secondhand and could not be confirmed. Sheriff Rick Wells: about $23M cut to his budget in year one and $50M total by year two. County baseline per staff (Feb 2026, secondhand): FY2026 general fund about $645M, property taxes about $327M.

races.name: Manatee County Water Quality Protection, Overdevelopment Prevention, Natural Lands Preservation and Public Preserves General Obligation Bonds ($75M, 0.16 mill)
races.summary: Authorizes the county to levy an added 0.16 mill property tax and issue up to $75M in general obligation bonds (20-year maturity, annual audits) to buy, improve and maintain environmental lands and conservation easements (including farmland development rights) that protect drinking water and water quality. It sits on top of the 2020 measure (0.15 mill, $50M cap, passed with about 71%). A no vote ends the program per the county natural-resources director; land already protected stays protected.

who_funds_yes.text: Political committee 'Protect Water, Preserve Land': $45,050 monetary + $8,926 in-kind per the Supervisor of Elections; donors Florida Wildlife Corridor Foundation $22,500, Trust for Public Land about $15,800, NCDG Management LLC (Sarasota; business not named in the filing) $10,000, and individuals; spending went mainly to Simmer House (Fort Myers) for marketing.

who_funds_no.text: No organized opposition committee found; opposition is individual voters (e.g. Trent Wayman) citing cost of living and distrust of county handling of funds.

supporters.text: Commissioners Mike Rahn and Tal Siddique (Siddique expects Amendment 3 supporters to back it); Conservation Florida; Keep Manatee Beautiful; Big Water Trust; League of Women Voters of Manatee County (supports, demands oversight fixes).

fiscal.text: About $16 per $100,000 of taxable value per year (TBT); about $34 a year on the median homestead per county staff (WUSF); on a $300,000 home the Observer says the bill rises from $45 to $93, a $48 increase. Collections under the 2020 levy: $7.6M (2023), $8.9M (2024), over $10M (2025); a county committee document cites $2.9M a year for maintenance. A county Inspector General audit found commingling of millage and other funds ('confusion and lack of transparency'); the county committed to separate funds and reimburse out-of-scope spending (per the League of Women Voters).
